clue.text: Go pale, receiving bill-it's a sham

indicators.note: receiving means the first piece takes the second one inside it

parts.note: to go pale is to fade
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone blanches on getting an invoice, suspecting it is a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is a false front, an outward show hiding the reality.

clue.text: Nominal leader takes van to island

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A figurehead drives a van over to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontman is a figurehead who represents an organisation while others hold the power.

clue.text: Vexation, but companion has a smile

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed, yet their partner is beaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or distress at failure or humiliation.

clue.text: In which clergyman might take the lead?

definitions.text: In which clergyman might take the lead?

parts.words: In which clergyman might take the lead?
parts.note: a dog is led by a lead clipped to its neckband; the stiff white band a priest wears around his neck shares the name

explanation.definitionFit: A clerical collar is the white band worn at the neck by priests, named after a dog's neckband.

clue.text: Added a couple of pages, then stopped

parts.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for page, so two pages are PP
stopped means ended

explanation.surface: Someone tacked two more pages onto a document and then quit writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Appended means attached at the end, a synonym of added.

clue.text: Horribly deep in L Ness, and feeling all prickly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Swimming far out in Loch Ness makes someone's skin tingle with fright.
explanation.walkthrough: L Ness reads as Loch Ness, a deep Scottish lake famous for its legendary monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins and needles is the tingling sensation in a limb as circulation returns.

clue.text: Am caught in lie over PC communication

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the whole construction is turned upwards
caught in means the first word is trapped inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out in a falsehood about a computer message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' gives LIAME; 'over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a message sent between computers.

clue.text: Make desperate attempt-entrance girl with Ecstasy

parts.note: a door is an entrance
Di is a girl's name
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A young woman at the door is carrying drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an all-or-nothing effort where failure is not an option.

clue.text: Is terrified of sadder outcome

indicators.note: outcome suggests the letters come out in a new form

explanation.surface: Someone fears a more unhappy result.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it greatly.

clue.text: I am to fine John for selfish attitude

parts.note: contracted to I'm
all right means fine
Jack is a familiar form of John

explanation.surface: Someone decides to impose a penalty on a man called John for being self-centred.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase expresses complacent indifference to others once one's own needs are met.

clue.text: Perhaps a German? No, he's Irish

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged some other way

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is German and is told he is Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals rearranging the letters of A GERMAN NO. An Orangeman is a member of the Orange Order, a Protestant society chiefly in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orangeman is a Protestant from Northern Ireland belonging to the Orange Order, so he is Irish.

clue.text: Sailor takes poem home

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A seaman carries a piece of verse back to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Commotion as rum is drunk during work

indicators.note: during places the rearranged spirit inside the word for work

parts.note: toil means hard work

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the spirit are reeling about

explanation.surface: There is a row at the workplace because spirits are being consumed on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is drunk' looks like the surface's verb but scrambles the spirit's letters; 'during' then sets them inside the word for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance or confusion, a synonym of commotion.

clue.text: Referred to everything you did in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the phrase is to be judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: everything is all, followed by you did

explanation.surface: Someone mentioned all the things another person got up to within earshot.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to mention indirectly, so alluded means referred to.

clue.text: Cancel girl-extremely unhelpful

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: extremely picks out the extreme ends of the word unhelpful, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone calls off an arrangement because a woman has been very obstructive.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, to cancel officially.

clue.text: Ruddy embarrassed

definitions.meaning: ruddy means flushed or reddish in complexion

explanation.definitionFit: Both a florid complexion and a blush of shame give a crimson countenance.

clue.text: On a charge after struggle in port

indicators.note: after a struggle the letters end up in disarray

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested after a fight at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: ANCHORAGE is a port city in Alaska, as well as any place to anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a place where ships can lie at anchor, hence a port or harbour.

clue.text: Policeman has information from the French about weapon

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: about means the word for from in French goes round the weapon

parts.note: de is French for from
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: An officer obtains intelligence from France concerning a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer.

clue.text: Discontinue meetings supporting villain

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A parliament is suspended to back a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue a parliament is to suspend its sessions without dissolving it.

clue.text: In car, hit 24 twice

parts.note: 24 refers to the answer to 24 down; a run is a cricketing addition to the score
over means left over, surplus, another sense of the answer to 24 down

explanation.surface: A motorist strikes the same thing again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies two synonyms in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over someone is to knock them down with a vehicle.

clue.text: Communist activist died in custody

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for died inside the word for custody

parts.note: being in care means being in someone's custody

explanation.surface: A party militant perished while held by the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a dedicated party worker, especially in a Communist organisation.

clue.text: Sadly, nun died somewhere in New Zealand

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A nun passed away at a place in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city on New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Mark of injury on a black beetle

parts.note: a scar is the mark a wound leaves
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: There is a wound mark on a dark insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Happy with what's included

explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable it means satisfied; on the first it means the matter something holds.

clue.text: He plays a small role in complex tragedy

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: An actor has a minor part in a complicated drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer hired for a non-speaking walk-on part.

clue.text: Doctor admitted being overwhelmed

parts.note: to own something is to admit or confess it

explanation.surface: A physician confessed to being swamped by work.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowned can mean swamped or submerged, as a sound is drowned out by a louder one.

clue.text: Arrive to help fasten down

indicators.note: help suggests the two words together supply the answer's letters, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to lend a hand securing something.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is concealed across 'arRIVE To'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fix firmly with metal pins, so to fasten down.

clue.text: Great conqueror had his technique

definitions.meaning: the Macedonian king who conquered much of the ancient world
a method of posture and movement named after F. M. ..., its inventor

explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian king called the Great shares his name with the founder of a posture method.

clue.text: Prohibit shelving in soldiers' quarters

parts.note: to bar is to prohibit
racks are frameworks of shelves

explanation.surface: Shelves are banned in the dormitories of an army camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are buildings housing troops.

clue.text: Irishman goes to church for a spirited meeting

parts.note: Sean is a typically Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman attends a church for a lively gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a gathering to contact the dead, a meeting with spirits.
